question: In an AMD on-campus software-intern interview, the candidate was asked to write a C program that prints the numbers 1 to 100 without using any loop (for, while or do-while).
lookingFor: Seeing that repetition can be expressed with recursion instead of loops
Defining a correct base case and recursive step
Awareness of stack depth and recursion cost
Knowing alternative tricks (macros, goto) and why they are worse
followUps: What is the space complexity of your solution and what limits the maximum n?
How would you print 1 to 100 without recursion and without loops?
What is tail-call optimisation and does C guarantee it?
How would you print the numbers in reverse using recursion?
